title: Whose Opinions Do Language Models Reflect?
benchmark_measurement: The benchmark measured the alignment of language model opinions with those of various US demographic groups, including religious groups. This was done by comparing the models' responses to multiple-choice questions from public opinion surveys (on topics like politics, science, and personal relationships) with the aggregated responses of specific religious affiliations (e.g., Protestant, Catholic, Jewish, Muslim) and levels of religious attendance.
findings: Base language models (LMs) are most aligned with the opinions of Protestant and Roman Catholic groups. In contrast, human-feedback-tuned models (e.g., OpenAI's text-davinci series) align more with people who are not religious or belong to religions like Buddhism, Islam, and Hinduism. The paper identifies that groups with high religious attendance and Mormons are poorly represented across all tested models. Furthermore, it finds inconsistencies in alignment; for example, even models that are generally liberal-leaning (like text-davinci-002 and text-davinci-003) express conservative views on the topic of religion.
references: Aher, G., Arriaga, R., and Kalai, A. Using large language models to simulate multiple humans. arXiv preprint arXiv:2208.10264, 2022.
